## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.


## Stage 1

2026-09-27 Entry

This week I learned a few techniques to improve the reproducibility of my 
data analysis.

1. Don't use machine-specific directories in my programming.

  When I need to use a file for my data analysis, the file is normally stored in 
  a digital "folder", and this "folder" is stored in my computer's storage. My
  computer's name will be different from the name of other people's computer so 
  if I were to write some programming that referred to a location in my computer, 
  the programming would not achieve the same result or cause an error if someone
  else were to run that program. 
  
  Instead, I can use a project file that is affiliated with a particular folder 
  that contains all the files associated with a data analysis. Then I can use
  the here() function to create objects that are associated with folders in the
  project. If someone obtains a copy of my repository, they will be able to 
  create that same object because the project will have the same name and the 
  folders in the project will have the same name. 
  
2. Use the renv package.
  The renv package does a few things. It creates a file that contains information
  about the version of all the packages that are being used in a project. The 
  second thing I can do with the renv package is to create separate lists of 
  packages for a project. That means I can use one version of a package for one 
  project and possibly use a different version of the same package for another
  project.
